output.review_comment: Removing `hours %= 24` and adding `{mins:02d}` are both correct and match the docstring. But changing `seconds // 60` to `round(seconds / 60)` goes against the documented spec. The docstring says leftover seconds are "dropped, never rounded up, so 119 seconds is shown as one minute," and with this change format_duration(119) returns "2m". The change exists only to satisfy test_ninety_minute_session (5399s -> "1h 30m"), which disagrees with the docstring (truncation gives "1h 29m"). The PR quietly sides with the test, doesn't mention the conflict, and leaves the docstring describing behavior the code no longer has. round() also rounds half to even (90s -> 2m, 150s -> 2m), and rounding up can over-report hours worked in a timesheet app. Please keep truncation and raise the test/docstring conflict with the teammate/HR. The test value may be a typo (e.g. meant 5400), or the spec may have changed. If it changed, update the docstring on purpose with an explicit rounding rule.
